items: An executive mailbox got shut off early once on an assistant's say-so and the exec was still very much in the role; the missed mail caused a real mess, so I treat exec accounts as fragile.
I never act on a departure before it actually exists on the HR record; 'the notice goes out later' means the person is still employed right now.
Routing executive mail to an assistant's box gives that assistant a quiet second window into leadership correspondence, which I consider a sensitive change on its own.
The CEO already signed off on winding down that exec mailbox with me, so the disable is just paperwork at this point and the EOD timing is fine.
We always close out the mailbox before the departure announcement so nothing leaks early; that is the standard sequence for executive transitions here.
The exec-departure-forward route to the assistant is the agreed continuity path so leadership mail keeps flowing while the seat is empty.
